texts: Deodoro da Fonseca was a Brazilian military leader and statesman, who played a crucial role in the 1889 military coup that overthrew the Brazilian Empire and established the First Brazilian Republic. He served as the first President of Brazil from 1889 to 1891. His presidency was marked by attempts to establish a strong centralized government, which ultimately led to his resignation amid political instability. Deodoro's tenure as president is considered an important yet turbulent period in Brazilian history, marking the transition from monarchy to republic.

Deodoro da Fonseca was a Brazilian general and politician, born on August 23, 1801. He is known for playing a significant role in the country's independence from Portugal. In 1889, he led a military coup that led to the abdication of Emperor Pedro II, marking the end of the Brazilian Empire and the establishment of the First Brazilian Republic, with Fonseca serving briefly as the first President of Brazil. Fonseca also served as the first Prime Minister of Brazil under the new republican government until a new president, Marshall Floriano Peixoto, was elected in 1891. After a short military career, he retired to his ranch and passed away on July 29, 1866.

Deodoro da Fonseca was a Brazilian military leader and statesman. He served as the second president of Brazil from 1891 to 1894, initially as a dictator from 1889 to 1891, after the abolition of the monarchy in 1889. A decorated general and prominent figure in the military, Fonseca implemented various reforms during his presidency, including the establishment of the Brazilian army's ranks, the creation of the Supreme Federal Tribunal, and a new constitution.

Deodoro da Fonseca (February 15, 1827 – August 11, 1892) was a Brazilian military officer and politician who played a significant role in the proclamation of the Brazilian Empire as a republic. He was the first President of Brazil, serving from November 15, 1889, to November 15, 1891. Known for his military skills, Fonseca led the Imperial Guard during the Brazilian Crown Prince's journey to Europe in 1871. He is also known for his role in the proclamation of the Republic of Brazil in 1888 and the subsequent military coup that led to the elimination of the monarchy in 1889, eventually becoming the first President of the new Republic. Despite serving as president, his tenure was brief due to political disagreements, and he retired to his farm in 1891.
